source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 8 (PDF 167-188), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 8 (Chemical Equilibrium) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 Macroscopic events are those phenomena which:
(Macroscopic events woh waqiyat hain jo:)

options.text: sirf electron microscope se dekhe ja sakte hain
sirf bonds tootne se mutalliq hain
nangi aankh se dekhe ja sakte hain

blocks.explanation: Macroscopic events nangi aankh se dekhe ja sakte hain, alag alag particles (zarraat) ko dekhe baghair (8.1.1).

book_ref.quote: phenomena that can be observed with the naked eye without considering the individual particles

blocks.prompt:
2 Which one of the following is a macroscopic property of a reaction?
(In mein se kaun si reaction ki macroscopic property hai?)

options.text: molecules mein atoms ki nayi tarteeb

blocks.explanation: Precipitate (tehshain) banna dekha ja sakta hai; baqi teen microscopic events hain (8.1.1, 8.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Change in colour, the evolution or absorption of heat, the formation of precipitate

blocks.prompt:
3 Which of the following is a microscopic event?
(In mein se kaun sa microscopic event hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bonds ka tootna aur banna nangi aankh se nahi dikhta, is liye yeh microscopic event hai (8.1.2).

book_ref.quote: The collisions between molecules, breaking and forming bonds, rearrangement of atoms

blocks.prompt:
4 An irreversible reaction stops when:
(Irreversible reaction kab ruk jata hai?)

options.text: forward aur reverse reactions ke rates barabar ho jayen

blocks.explanation: Irreversible reaction mein reactants poori tarah khatam ho jate hain; limiting reactant (kam parne wala reactant) khatam hone par yeh ruk jata hai (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Such reactions stop when the limiting reactant is used up.

blocks.prompt:
5 At chemical equilibrium, the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are:
(Chemical equilibrium par forward aur reverse reactions ke rates kaise hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Equilibrium par concentrations constant ho jati hain aur forward aur reverse rates barabar ho jate hain (8.1).

book_ref.quote: At this point, the concentrations of reactants and products become constant

blocks.prompt:
6 In the equation PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), the double arrow shows that the reaction is:
(PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) mein double arrow kya batata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Double arrow batata hai ke reaction reversible (dono taraf chalne wala) hai (8.1).

book_ref.quote: The double arrow tells that the reaction is reversible.

blocks.prompt:
7 A reversible reaction reaches chemical equilibrium when it is carried out in a container which:
(Reversible reaction kis qisam ke bartan mein chemical equilibrium tak pohanchta hai?)

options.text: kisi substance ko andar aane ya bahar jaane na de
sirf reactants ko andar aane de

blocks.explanation: Equilibrium aise bartan mein banta hai jo kisi bhi shamil substance ko andar aane ya bahar jaane na de (8.1).

book_ref.quote: in a container which prevents the entry or escape of any of the substances involved

blocks.text: 8.2 Reversible reactions, microscopic events and dynamic equilibrium

blocks.prompt:
8 When steam and carbon monoxide are mixed, the forward reaction has its maximum rate:
(Jab steam aur carbon monoxide milaye jate hain to forward reaction ka rate sab se zyada kab hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Shuru mein H₂O aur CO ke darmiyan har second takraon ki tadad sab se zyada hoti hai, is liye forward rate shuru mein sab se zyada hota hai (8.2).

book_ref.quote: Therefore, the forward reaction has its maximum rate at the beginning.

blocks.prompt:
9 In the reaction H₂O(g) + CO(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + CO₂(g), the products formed are:
(Reaction H₂O(g) + CO(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + CO₂(g) mein kaun se products bante hain?)
blocks.explanation: CO aur H₂O ke bonds toot kar naye bonds bante hain aur H₂ aur CO₂ paida hoti hain (8.2).

book_ref.quote: As H₂O and CO are gradually used up, the forward reaction slows down.

blocks.prompt:
10 At the start of the reaction between steam and CO, the rate of the reverse reaction is:
(Steam aur CO ke reaction ke shuru mein reverse reaction ka rate kaisa hota hai?)

options.text: sab se zyada, phir sifar tak kam
kam, phir barhta hai aur aakhir mein constant
shuru se hi forward rate ke barabar

blocks.explanation: Shuru mein reverse rate kam hota hai, H₂ aur CO₂ jama hone se ahista ahista barhta hai, aur aakhir mein constant ho jata hai (8.2).

book_ref.quote: at the start, the rate of the reverse reaction is low, gradually increases, and finally becomes constant

blocks.prompt:
11 At the state of chemical equilibrium:
(Chemical equilibrium ki haalat mein:)

options.text: saare reactants khatam ho chuke hote hain
forward reaction ruk chuka hota hai

blocks.explanation: Chemical equilibrium par reaction mixture ki composition (banawat) nahi badalti aur forward aur reverse rates barabar hote hain (8.2).

book_ref.quote: composition of the reaction mixture does not change and forward and reverse rates are equal

blocks.prompt:
12 For the general reaction A ⇌ B, at the equilibrium position the concentration of A compared with that of B:
(General reaction A ⇌ B mein equilibrium par A ki concentration B ke muqable mein:)

options.text: barabar, kam ya zyada ho sakti hai

blocks.explanation: Figure 8.1 dikhata hai ke equilibrium par reactant aur product barabar bhi ho sakte hain, ya reactant kam ya zyada bhi ho sakta hai (8.2).

book_ref.quote: the concentrations of the reactant and the product may be equal as shown in Figure 8.1 (a)

blocks.prompt:
13 In all the concentration-time graphs of Figure 8.1, after equilibrium is established the concentrations:
(Figure 8.1 ke tamam concentration-time graphs mein equilibrium banne ke baad concentrations:)
blocks.explanation: Tamam graphs mein equilibrium banne ke baad concentrations constant ho jati hain (8.2).

book_ref.quote: for all of these graphs, it is clear that after the equilibrium is established, the concentrations become constant

blocks.prompt:
14 Chemical equilibrium is called dynamic because:
(Chemical equilibrium ko dynamic kyun kaha jata hai?)

options.text: reaction bilkul ruk chuka hota hai
molecules dono taraf barabar rate se react karte rehte hain

blocks.explanation: Alag alag molecules musalsal react karte rehte hain lekin forward aur reverse rates barabar hote hain, is liye equilibrium dynamic (mutaharrik) hai (8.2).

book_ref.quote: The system is dynamic because the individual molecules are constantly reacting

blocks.text: 8.3 Relation between macroscopic and microscopic events

blocks.prompt:
15 Macroscopic events are the result of:
(Macroscopic events kis cheez ka nateeja hain?)

options.text: bohat se aik saath hone wale microscopic events

blocks.explanation: Macroscopic events bohat se aik waqt mein hone wale microscopic events ka nateeja hain (8.3).

book_ref.quote: Macroscopic events are the result of multiple simultaneous microscopic events.

blocks.prompt:
16 The rates of the forward and reverse reactions in an equilibrium system are affected by:
(Equilibrium system mein forward aur reverse reactions ke rates kis se mutassir hote hain?)
blocks.explanation: Takrao forward aur reverse rates ko badalte hain, jo activation energy aur bahari factors se mutassir hote hain (8.3).

book_ref.quote: These collisions change the rates of forward and reverse reactions

blocks.prompt:
17 The escape of liquid molecules from the surface into the gaseous phase in a closed container is called:
(Band bartan mein liquid ke molecules ka surface se gas phase mein nikal jana kya kehlata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Surface ke qareeb kaafi energy wale molecules gas phase mein nikal jate hain; isay evaporation (bukharat) kehte hain (8.3).

book_ref.quote: some of the liquid molecules near the surface have enough energy to escape into the gaseous phase

blocks.prompt:
18 Vapour molecules colliding with the liquid surface and being captured again by the liquid is called:
(Vapour ke molecules ka liquid surface se takra kar dobara liquid mein qaid ho jana kya kehlata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Vapour molecules ka dobara liquid mein aa jana condensation (takseef) hai (8.3).

book_ref.quote: molecules in vapour phase can also collide with the liquid surface and be captured again by the liquid

blocks.prompt:
19 When a liquid and its vapour are at dynamic equilibrium in a closed container:
(Jab band bartan mein liquid aur us ki vapour dynamic equilibrium par hon to:)

options.text: evaporation aur condensation ke rates barabar hote hain

blocks.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium par evaporation aur condensation barabar rate se hote hain aur diye gaye temperature par vapour pressure constant rehta hai (8.3).

book_ref.quote: At dynamic equilibrium, the vapor pressure remains constant at a given temperature

blocks.prompt:
20 When the temperature of a liquid in equilibrium with its vapour is raised, the system reaches a new equilibrium with:
(Jab apni vapour ke saath equilibrium wale liquid ka temperature barhaya jaye to naya equilibrium kis ke saath banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Zyada temperature average kinetic energy aur evaporation rate barhata hai, is liye naye equilibrium par vapour pressure zyada hota hai (8.3).

book_ref.quote: Finally, the system will reach a new state of dynamic equilibrium, with a higher equilibrium vapor pressure.

blocks.text: 8.4 Dynamic equilibrium between two physical states

blocks.prompt:
21 In a dynamic equilibrium:
(Dynamic equilibrium mein:)

options.text: tabdeeliyan jaari rehti hain lekin net tabdeeli nazar nahi aati
sirf forward tabdeeli jaari rehti hai
net tabdeeli sab se zyada hoti hai

blocks.explanation: Agarche tabdeeliyan musalsal hoti rehti hain, poore system mein koi net (khalis) tabdeeli nazar nahi aati (8.4).

book_ref.quote: no net change in the system as a whole is observed

blocks.prompt:
22 Ice and water coexist in dynamic equilibrium at:
(Barf aur pani kis temperature par dynamic equilibrium mein aik saath mojood rehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: 0 °C par barf aur pani aik saath rehte hain; pani barf banta hai aur barf pani, dono barabar rate se (8.4).

book_ref.quote: For example, at 0 °C, ice and water coexist in equilibrium.

blocks.prompt:
23 The state of equilibrium applies only to:
(Equilibrium ki haalat sirf kis par laagu hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Equilibrium ki haalat sirf reversible reactions par laagu hoti hai (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The state of equilibrium only applies to reversible reactions.

blocks.prompt:
24 Equilibrium cannot be established when calcium carbonate is heated in an open vessel because:
(Khule bartan mein calcium carbonate garam karne par equilibrium kyun nahi banta?)

options.text: aik product bartan se bahar nikal jata hai

blocks.explanation: Equilibrium ke liye band bartan zaroori hai; koi reactant ya product bahar na nikle. Khule bartan mein CO₂ nikal jati hai (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The equilibrium can be established only if the reaction vessel is closed.

blocks.prompt:
25 The state of equilibrium in a reversible reaction can be approached:
(Reversible reaction mein equilibrium ki haalat tak kaise pohancha ja sakta hai?)

options.text: sirf reactants se shuru kar ke
sirf products se shuru kar ke
dono taraf se, reactants ya products se shuru kar ke

blocks.explanation: Equilibrium tak dono taraf se pohancha ja sakta hai, chahe reactants se shuru karein ya products se (8.6).

book_ref.quote: can be approached from either side whether we start with reactants or products

blocks.prompt:
26 The value of the equilibrium constant of a reaction depends on:
(Kisi reaction ke equilibrium constant ki qeemat kis par munhasir hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kc shuru ki concentrations par munhasir nahi; yeh constant hai aur sirf temperature par munhasir hai (8.6).

book_ref.quote: rather it is constants and depends on temperature only

blocks.prompt:
27 A catalyst added to a reversible reaction:
(Reversible reaction mein catalyst daalne se:)

options.text: equilibrium jaldi qaim karne mein madad deta hai
equilibrium ko daayen taraf khiska deta hai

blocks.explanation: Catalyst equilibrium position ya constant nahi badalta; yeh equilibrium jaldi qaim karne mein madad deta hai (8.6).

book_ref.quote: It helps to attain the equilibrium earlier.

blocks.prompt:
28 For CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g), the equilibrium constant expression is:
(CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g) ke liye equilibrium constant expression kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khalis solids Kc expression mein shamil nahi hote, is liye sirf CO₂(g) aati hai: Kc = [CO₂] (8.6).

book_ref.quote: their concentrations are not included in the equilibrium constant expression

blocks.prompt:
29 With respect to the physical states of reactants and products, chemical equilibrium is of:
(Reactants aur products ki physical haalat ke lihaz se chemical equilibrium ki kitni qismein hain?)
blocks.explanation: Physical haalat ke lihaz se do qismein hain: homogeneous aur heterogeneous (8.7).

book_ref.quote: With respect to the physical states of reactants and products, there are two types

blocks.prompt:
30 An equilibrium in which all reactants and products are in the same phase is called:
(Woh equilibrium jis mein tamam reactants aur products aik hi phase mein hon kya kehlata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Jab tamam reactants aur products aik hi phase mein hon to equilibrium homogeneous (yaksaan) hai (8.7.1).

book_ref.quote: An equilibrium system in which all of the reactants and products are in the same phase.

blocks.prompt:
31 Which of the following is a homogeneous equilibrium?
(In mein se kaun sa homogeneous equilibrium hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ mein har substance gas hai, is liye homogeneous; baqi mein solids aur gases dono hain (8.7.1).

book_ref.quote: The following are examples of homogeneous equilibria:

blocks.prompt:
32 A heterogeneous equilibrium is one in which the reactants and products are:
(Heterogeneous equilibrium mein reactants aur products:)
blocks.explanation: Heterogeneous equilibrium mein reactants aur products aik se zyada phases mein hote hain (8.7).

book_ref.quote: An equilibrium in which the reactants and products are in more than one phases

blocks.prompt:
33 Which of these is an example of heterogeneous equilibrium?
(In mein se kaun si heterogeneous equilibrium ki misaal hai?)
blocks.explanation: Iron aur Fe₃O₄ solid hain jab ke H₂O aur H₂ gases: aik se zyada phase (8.7).

book_ref.quote: The following are examples of heterogeneous equilibrium:

blocks.prompt:
34 For C(s) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + H₂(g), the equilibrium constant expression is:
(C(s) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + H₂(g) ke liye equilibrium constant expression kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Solid carbon expression se nikal diya jata hai (Keep in Mind, 8.6), is liye Kc = [CO][H₂]/[H₂O] (8.7).

book_ref.quote: The following are examples of heterogeneous equilibrium:

blocks.prompt:
35 The esterification CH₃COOH(l) + C₂H₅OH(l) ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅(l) + H₂O(l) is a homogeneous equilibrium because:
(Esterification CH₃COOH(l) + C₂H₅OH(l) ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅(l) + H₂O(l) homogeneous equilibrium kyun hai?)

options.text: tamam substances liquid phase mein hain

blocks.explanation: Chaaron substances aik hi (liquid) phase mein hain, is liye equilibrium homogeneous hai (8.7.1).

book_ref.quote: The following are examples of homogeneous equilibria:

blocks.text: 8.8 Equilibrium constant and position of equilibrium

blocks.prompt:
36 The relation between equilibrium concentrations that leads to the equilibrium constant was discovered in 1864 by:
(Equilibrium constant tak le jaane wala taaluq 1864 mein kis ne daryaft kiya?)
blocks.explanation: 1864 mein Norwegian chemists C. Guldberg aur P. Waage ne bohat se equilibrium mixtures naap kar yeh constant ratio daryaft kiya (8.8).

book_ref.quote: In 1864, the Norwegian chemists C. Guldberg (1836–1902) and P. Waage (1833–1900)

blocks.prompt:
37 In the law of mass action, the term 'active mass' means:
(Law of mass action mein 'active mass' se kya muraad hai?)
blocks.explanation: Active mass se muraad molar concentration hai, jo moles dm⁻³ mein likhi jati hai (8.8).

book_ref.quote: By the term active mass, we mean the molar concentration.

blocks.prompt:
38 In an equilibrium constant expression, square brackets [ ] stand for:
(Equilibrium constant expression mein square brackets [ ] kis cheez ko zahir karte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Molar concentration (moles dm⁻³) square brackets [ ] se zahir ki jati hai (8.8).

book_ref.quote: This concentration is expressed by square brackets [ ].

blocks.prompt:
39 According to the law of mass action, the rate of a reaction is directly proportional to:
(Law of mass action ke mutabiq reaction ka rate kis ke directly proportional hai?)

options.text: reactants ke active masses, coefficients ki power ke saath

blocks.explanation: Rate reactants ke active masses ke directly proportional hai, jin par balanced equation ke coefficients ki power hoti hai (8.8).

book_ref.quote: The rate of the chemical reaction is directly proportional to the active masses of the reactants

blocks.prompt:
40 In terms of the forward rate constant kf and the reverse rate constant kr, Kc is equal to:
(Forward rate constant kf aur reverse rate constant kr ke lihaz se Kc kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: Equilibrium par kf[A][B] = kr[C][D], is liye kf/kr = [C][D]/[A][B] = Kc (8.8).

book_ref.quote: The left side of this equation is the ratio of two rate constants

blocks.prompt:
41 For a reversible reaction the forward rate constant is 6.0 × 10⁻³ and the reverse rate constant is 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ (same units). Kc is:
(Aik reversible reaction ka forward rate constant 6.0 × 10⁻³ aur reverse rate constant 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ hai (aik jaisi units). Kc kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: The left side of this equation is the ratio of two rate constants

blocks.prompt:
42 For A + B ⇌ C + D, the rate of the forward reaction is written as:
(A + B ⇌ C + D ke liye forward reaction ka rate kaise likha jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Law of mass action se forward reaction ka rate ∝ [A][B] = kf[A][B] (8.8).

book_ref.quote: ‘kf’ is the proportionality constant, and is known as forward rate constant.

blocks.prompt:
43 For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the equilibrium constant expression is:
(N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) ke liye equilibrium constant expression kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har concentration par us ka coefficient power banta hai: Kc = [NH₃]²/[N₂][H₂]³ (8.8.1).

book_ref.quote: where a, b, c and d are the coefficients of balanced equation.

blocks.prompt:
44 For 2N₂O₅(g) ⇌ 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g), the equilibrium constant expression is:
(2N₂O₅(g) ⇌ 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g) ke liye equilibrium constant expression kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Products upar, reactants neeche, har aik par coefficient ki power: Kc = [NO₂]⁴[O₂]/[N₂O₅]² (8.8.1).

book_ref.quote: This equation is known as equilibrium constant expression.

blocks.prompt:
45 An esterification mixture of 250 cm³ at equilibrium contains 0.100 mol ethanoic acid, 0.050 mol ethanol, 0.200 mol ethyl ethanoate and 0.100 mol water. Kc is:
(250 cm³ esterification mixture mein equilibrium par 0.100 mol ethanoic acid, 0.050 mol ethanol, 0.200 mol ethyl ethanoate aur 0.100 mol pani hai. Kc kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Concentrations: acid 0.400, ethanol 0.200, ester 0.800, pani 0.400 mol dm⁻³. Kc = (0.800 × 0.400)/(0.400 × 0.200) = 4.0, koi unit nahi (8.8.1).

book_ref.quote: Use this data to calculate a value of Kc for this reaction.

blocks.prompt:
46 A mixture of 0.0600 mol dm⁻³ propanone and 0.0600 mol dm⁻³ HCN reaches equilibrium with 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ of product. The equilibrium concentration of propanone is:
(0.0600 mol dm⁻³ propanone aur 0.0600 mol dm⁻³ HCN ka mixture equilibrium par 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ product deta hai. Equilibrium par propanone ki concentration kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har mol product ke liye 1 mol propanone kharch hota hai: 0.0600 − 0.0200 = 0.0400 mol dm⁻³ (8.8.1).

book_ref.quote: A mixture of 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ propanone and 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ hydrogen cyanide is left to reach equilibrium

blocks.prompt:
47 Using the data of the previous question (propanone and HCN each 0.0400 mol dm⁻³, product 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ at equilibrium), Kc is:
(Pichle sawal ke data se (equilibrium par propanone aur HCN har aik 0.0400 mol dm⁻³, product 0.0200 mol dm⁻³), Kc kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kc = 0.0200/(0.0400 × 0.0400) = 12.5; unit (mol dm⁻³)⁻¹ = mol⁻¹ dm³ hai (8.8.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: A mixture of 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ propanone and 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ hydrogen cyanide is left to reach equilibrium

blocks.prompt:
48 Kc has no units when:
(Kc ki koi unit kab nahi hoti?)

options.text: balanced equation mein reactants aur products ke moles barabar hon

blocks.explanation: Jab balanced equation mein reactants aur products ke moles barabar hon to units cancel ho jati hain (8.8.2).

book_ref.quote: When the number of moles of reactants and products in balanced chemical equations are equal

blocks.prompt:
49 The unit of Kc for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) is:
(N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) ke Kc ki unit kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: (mol dm⁻³)²/[(mol dm⁻³)(mol dm⁻³)³] = 1/(mol dm⁻³)² = mol⁻² dm⁶ (8.8.2).

book_ref.quote: In the synthesis of NH₃ by Haber’s process, the units of reactants and products are not cancelled.

blocks.prompt:
50 The unit of Kc for 2N₂O₅(g) ⇌ 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g) is:
(2N₂O₅(g) ⇌ 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g) ke Kc ki unit kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kc = [NO₂]⁴[O₂]/[N₂O₅]² ki unit (mol dm⁻³)⁵/(mol dm⁻³)² = (mol dm⁻³)³ = mol³ dm⁻⁹ (8.8.2).

book_ref.quote: When the number of moles are unequal, then value of equilibrium constant depend upon the units

blocks.prompt:
51 Which reaction has an equilibrium constant Kc with no units?
(Kis reaction ke Kc ki koi unit nahi?)
blocks.explanation: H₂O + CO ⇌ H₂ + CO₂ mein 2 mol reactants se 2 mol products bante hain, is liye units cancel ho jati hain (8.8.2).

book_ref.quote: The ester formation reaction happens in solution state

blocks.prompt:
52 For the general reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, the power of [A] in the Kc expression is:
(General reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD ke Kc expression mein [A] ki power kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har concentration par balanced equation ka coefficient power hota hai, is liye [A] par power a hai (8.8, book correction).

book_ref.quote: The power of [A] is printed as n. It is the coefficient a of A in the balanced equation

blocks.prompt:
53 How many different types of quantities may be used to calculate the equilibrium constants of a reversible reaction?
(Reversible reaction ke equilibrium constants nikalne ke liye kitni qisam ki quantities istemal ho sakti hain?)
blocks.explanation: Concentrations, partial pressures, moles ki tadad aur mole fractions se Kc, Kp, Kn aur Kx bante hain (8.9).

book_ref.quote: There are four different types of quantities which may be used to calculate the equilibrium constants

blocks.prompt:
54 The equilibrium constant written in terms of partial pressures of gases is:
(Gases ke partial pressures ke lihaz se likha gaya equilibrium constant kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Jab concentrations partial pressures ki shakal mein hon to constant Kp hota hai (8.9).

book_ref.quote: When the concentrations are expressed in terms of partial pressures (p) for gaseous reactants and products

blocks.prompt:
55 Kx is the equilibrium constant expressed in terms of:
(Kx kis cheez ke lihaz se likha gaya equilibrium constant hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kx reactants aur products ke mole fractions (X) istemal karta hai (8.9).

book_ref.quote: When the concentrations are expressed in terms of mole fractions, (X) then

blocks.prompt:
56 In Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn, Δn for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) is:
(Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn mein 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) ke liye Δn kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Δn = gaseous products ke moles − gaseous reactants ke moles = 2 − 3 = −1 (8.9).

book_ref.quote: Δn = Difference of number of moles of products and reactants in the balanced chemical equation

blocks.prompt:
57 For which reaction is Δn = +3?
(Kis reaction ke liye Δn = +3 hai?)
blocks.explanation: 2N₂O₅ ⇌ 4NO₂ + O₂ ke liye: Δn = (4 + 1) − 2 = +3 (8.9).

book_ref.quote: Δn = Difference of number of moles of products and reactants in the balanced chemical equation

blocks.prompt:
58 Kp = Kc = Kx = Kn when:
(Kp = Kc = Kx = Kn kab hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Agar balanced equation mein reactants aur products ke moles barabar hon to Δn = 0 aur tamam constants barabar hote hain (8.9).

book_ref.quote: Hence, whichever concentration units are used, the equilibrium constants are same.

blocks.prompt:
59 The relation between Kp and Kx is:
(Kp aur Kx ka taaluq kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Section 8.9 ki equation (6): Kp = Kx(P)^Δn, jahan P system ka pressure hai (8.9).

book_ref.quote: The relationships between these equilibrium constants are as follows:

blocks.prompt:
60 The correct relation between Kp and Kn is:
(Kp aur Kn ka sahi taaluq kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har partial pressure p = (n/N) × P hai, is liye Kp = Kn(P/N)^Δn (8.9, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Each partial pressure is p = (n / N) × P, so equation (7) should be Kp = Kn (P/N)^Δn.
